subject: design-technology
title: Arduino and the Microcontroller
welcome_lead: A microcontroller for the rest of us — open hardware since 2005.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: Arduino microcontroller platform and embedded systems.

concepts.def: Open-source microcontroller platform, launched 2005, Ivrea, Italy.
Single-chip computer with CPU, memory, I/O for embedded use.
Pin set to HIGH (3.3 V or 5 V) or LOW (0 V).
Pin reading a voltage as a digital number via ADC.
Pulse Width Modulation — duty cycle simulates analogue output.

walkthroughs.body_html: Arduino launched at Interaction Design Institute Ivrea (Italy) in 2005, designed by Massimo Banzi and team. Open-source hardware and a simple IDE made microcontrollers accessible to designers.
Arduino Uno has 14 digital I/O pins and 6 analogue input pins. The 10-bit ADC reads 0-5 V as 0-1023. PWM on six pins simulates analogue output by varying duty cycle.

Designers use Arduino to prototype interactive products — lighting that responds to motion, weather stations, robot controllers. From prototype it can graduate to a custom PCB carrying the same ATmega chip.
